problem.title: Design a 100MB-File Code Editor Text Buffer with O(log N) Edits, Undo & Line Index
problem.tagline: Architect a 60fps 100 MB code editor buffer using a 64 KB-chunked Red-Black Piece Tree, descending multi-cursor edits, and incremental Tree-sitter deltas.
problem.purpose: Design a high-performance text buffer that supports <0.1 ms edits, O(log P) line lookups, O(1) Undo, and crash-safe saves on 100 MB+ files.

spark.summary: A 64 KB-chunked Red-Black Piece Tree with augmented (left_len, left_lf) counts delivers <0.1 ms edits, O(log P) line slicing, 64B Undo deltas, and lock-free worker snapshots.
spark.keyTakeaway: Chunk 100 MB mmap files into 64 KB immutable pieces, apply multi-cursor edits in descending offset order, and save via .tmp + fsync + atomic rename.
spark.byteSummary:
Modern code editors (VS Code, Zed, Neovim) must open 100 MB+ minified bundles or log files in <100 ms, sustain 1,000-cursor edits inside a 16 ms (60fps) frame budget, serve `O(log P)` line/column lookups for virtualized viewport rendering, and run background Tree-sitter parsing and LSP diagnostics without blocking the UI thread.

The architecture centers on a **64 KB-Chunked Red-Black Piece Tree**: the 100 MB file is memory-mapped or lazily paged in 64 KB chunks as an immutable Original Buffer, while keystrokes append to an Add Buffer. Each tree node caches `(left_len, left_lf)` for `O(log P)` offset and line-number navigation. A persistent **Command Undo/Redo Stack** stores ~64-byte inverse piece deltas, while path-copied immutable tree snapshots feed background Tree-sitter incremental reparsing (`<3 ms`) and LSP workers lock-free.

To stay resilient in production, the buffer guards UTF-16 surrogate and CRLF boundaries, compacts fragmented trees past 50,000 pieces on idle frames, logs unsaved deltas every 2s to a crash-recovery WAL, and saves via `.tmp` streaming + `fsync()` + atomic `rename()`.

learningJourney.title: Sizing 100 MB Files, 16 ms 60fps Frames & 1,000-Cursor Edits
learningJourney.purpose: Establish <100 ms file-open, <1 ms multi-cursor edit, and <50 MB overhead budgets for 100 MB files.

explanation.foundation: Target: open a 100 MB file (~2M lines) in `<100 ms`, execute 1,000 simultaneous cursor edits in `<2 ms`, and render 60fps (`<16 ms/frame`).
explanation.core: Splitting the 100 MB Original Buffer into ~1,600 x 64 KB chunks keeps initial Piece Tree build under 30 ms and avoids allocating 2,000,000 per-line string objects (~320 MB heap bloat).
explanation.deepDive: Virtualizing the viewport renders only the ~60 visible lines via `O(log P)` `get_line_content(row)` calls—never materializing the whole file.

learningJourney.title: Piece Tree + Incremental Tree-sitter + Background LSP Snapshots
learningJourney.purpose: Coordinate UI-thread Piece Tree edits with lock-free immutable snapshots for Tree-sitter and LSP workers.

explanation.foundation: Every keystroke mutates the Red-Black Piece Tree on the UI thread in `<100 us` and pushes a ~64B inverse command onto the Undo stack.
explanation.core: The buffer emits an exact `(start_byte, old_end_byte, new_end_byte)` edit delta to **Tree-sitter** so syntax highlighting reparses only the modified AST subtree in `<3 ms`.
explanation.deepDive: Background LSP and search threads read an immutable path-copied tree root snapshot—never blocking UI typing.

cards.label: Exact Byte Deltas
cards.detail: Tree-sitter needs exact byte offsets and (row, col) points—both served in O(log P) by the Piece Tree.

cards.label: Lock-Free Background Search
cards.detail: Regex Find-in-File scans an immutable snapshot across worker threads without locking the editor.

cards.label: Zero String Concat
cards.detail: Tokens and viewport lines read directly from buffer slices.

learningJourney.title: Reverse-Sorted Multi-Cursor Edits & O(log P) Line-Offset Lookup
learningJourney.purpose: Apply multi-cursor edits in descending offset order so earlier offsets stay valid without shifting.

explanation.foundation: If 1,000 cursors edit in ascending offset order, edit #1 shifts the byte offsets of edits #2..#1,000!
explanation.deepDive: Checking `off_lo + del_lo > off_hi` prevents corrupt overlapping deletions when two cursors converge on the same word.

sectionDiagram.title: Reverse-Sorted Multi-Cursor Edits & O(log P) Line-Offset Lookup

cards.label: Descending Order Invariant
cards.detail: Mutating from bottom-of-file upward means lower offsets remain 100% valid without recalculation.

cards.label: Atomic Multi-Cursor Undo
cards.detail: Wrap all 1,000 cursor deltas in one composite Undo group so Ctrl+Z reverts all cursors together.

cards.label: Overlap Merge
cards.detail: Merge adjacent/overlapping selections before applying edits.

sectionDiagram.summary: Descending-offset sorting, overlap checks, and composite Undo grouping execute 1,000-cursor edits cleanly.
sectionDiagram.caption: Descending-offset sorting, overlap checks, and composite Undo grouping execute 1,000-cursor edits cleanly.

learningJourney.title: Handling 10 MB Single-Line Minified JS Without Freezing Tokenizers
learningJourney.purpose: Bound viewport horizontal slicing and tokenizer line caps when a single line spans millions of characters.

explanation.foundation: A minified `.min.js` file has 1 line that is 10,000,000 characters long—rendering or regex-tokenizing the whole line freezes the UI!
explanation.core: Cap `get_line_slice(line, col_start, col_end)` to the visible horizontal viewport (`~300 chars`) using `O(log P)` offset slicing, and disable expensive regex syntax highlighting on lines `> 20,000 chars`.
explanation.deepDive: Because Piece Tree nodes track `left_len`, slicing columns `[500_000 .. 500_300]` on a 10M-char single line still runs in `O(log P)`.

sectionDiagram.title: Handling 10 MB Single-Line Minified JS Without Freezing Tokenizers

cards.label: Horizontal Virtualization
cards.detail: Never materialize a 10M-char line string just to draw 200 visible columns.

cards.label: Syntax Guardrail
cards.detail: Falling back to plain monochrome text on >20K-char lines prevents catastrophic regex backtracking.

cards.label: 64 KB Chunk Limit
cards.detail: Even on a 1-line 100 MB file, 64 KB chunking keeps individual piece operations tiny.

sectionDiagram.summary: Horizontal O(log P) viewport slicing and 20K-char tokenizer caps keep 10 MB minified single-line files responsive.
sectionDiagram.caption: Horizontal O(log P) viewport slicing and 20K-char tokenizer caps keep 10 MB minified single-line files responsive.

learningJourney.title: CRLF Split Guards, UTF-16 Surrogate Safety & Idle Piece Compaction
learningJourney.purpose: Protect line-feed invariants across piece boundaries and compact >50K-piece trees without frame drops.

explanation.foundation: Cross-piece `\r` + `\n` boundaries and fragmented trees from 100K Find-and-Replace edits can skew line numbers or bloat depth.
explanation.core: Enforce CRLF-atomic split points (never split between `\r` and `\n`), validate UTF-16 surrogate boundaries, and compact contiguous Add-Buffer pieces in 2 ms time-sliced idle chunks when `P > 50,000`.
explanation.deepDive: Time-slicing compaction inside `requestIdleCallback` ensures defragmentation never causes a visible typing stutter.

sectionDiagram.title: CRLF Split Guards, UTF-16 Surrogate Safety & Idle Piece Compaction

cards.label: CRLF Boundary Rule
cards.detail: Checking adjacent piece ends handles mixed LF/CRLF files without corrupting line numbers.

cards.label: Budgeted Compaction
cards.detail: Spending at most 2 ms per idle frame keeps typing latency untouched.

cards.label: Bounded Add Buffer
cards.detail: Compaction also discards dead deleted slices during full file saves.

sectionDiagram.summary: Encoding-safe split guards and 2 ms idle-time compaction protect line accuracy and prevent tree bloat.
sectionDiagram.caption: Encoding-safe split guards and 2 ms idle-time compaction protect line accuracy and prevent tree bloat.

learningJourney.title: 2-Second Edit WAL Recovery & Safe Atomic Mmap Re-Binding
learningJourney.purpose: Recover unsaved edits after power loss and save 100 MB files without corrupting active mmap buffers.

explanation.foundation: Power loss or OOM kills between saves must not lose hours of unsaved edits.
explanation.core: Flush edit deltas every 2 seconds to a local recovery WAL keyed by `(file_path, base_sha256)`. On save, stream pieces to `.tmp`, `fsync()`, `rename()`, and swap the Original Buffer cleanly.
explanation.deepDive: If the file changed externally on disk while unsaved WAL deltas exist, surface a 3-way diff instead of blindly overwriting.

sectionDiagram.title: 2-Second Edit WAL Recovery & Safe Atomic Mmap Re-Binding

cards.label: Base Hash Verification
cards.detail: Checking base_sha256 before replaying WAL deltas prevents applying edits onto an externally modified file.

cards.label: Atomic Mmap Swap
cards.detail: Unmap the old Original Buffer only after .tmp rename succeeds and the new Piece Tree root is bound.

cards.label: Truncate WAL on Save
cards.detail: Clear the recovery journal immediately after atomic rename completes.

sectionDiagram.summary: Hash-verified 2s WAL journals and atomic .tmp-to-mmap swaps guarantee crash recovery and safe 100 MB saves.
sectionDiagram.caption: Hash-verified 2s WAL journals and atomic .tmp-to-mmap swaps guarantee crash recovery and safe 100 MB saves.

learningJourney.title: Monitoring Keystroke Frame Drops, Piece Depth & Memory Footprint
learningJourney.purpose: Track p99 keystroke-to-paint latency, piece count, and Tree-sitter parse budgets in production.

explanation.foundation: IDE sluggishness often hides in a single slow extension or pathological regex on large files.
explanation.deepDive: Automatically shed non-essential LSP inlays or regex decorators if frame time exceeds 16 ms for 5 consecutive frames.

sectionDiagram.title: Monitoring Keystroke Frame Drops, Piece Depth & Memory Footprint

cards.label: Graceful Large-File Mode
cards.detail: Automatically disable expensive regex/inlay decorators above 50 MB while keeping Piece Tree edits fast.

cards.label: Compaction Telemetry
cards.detail: Track piece count before/after idle compaction to tune chunk thresholds.

cards.label: Zero-Content Logging
cards.detail: Never log user source code—emit only timings, byte sizes, and piece counts.

sectionDiagram.summary: Tracking 16 ms frame budgets, piece counts, and incremental AST times keeps large-file editing smooth.
sectionDiagram.caption: Tracking 16 ms frame budgets, piece counts, and incremental AST times keeps large-file editing smooth.

knowledgeChecks.question: When applying 1,000 simultaneous multi-cursor edits to a Piece Tree, why should they be sorted in **descending** offset order?

options.text: Mutating higher byte offsets first leaves all lower byte offsets unchanged, avoiding O(C^2) offset recalculations.
options.feedback: Correct! Applying edits from bottom-of-file upward keeps every earlier cursor offset valid.

options.text: Because Red-Black trees can only delete nodes from the right leaf.
options.feedback: Red-Black trees support deletions anywhere; descending order preserves cursor offsets.

options.text: Because Tree-sitter requires edits in reverse chronological order.
options.feedback: Tree-sitter accepts sequential edit deltas; descending order is for multi-cursor offset stability.

options.text: To force the Add Buffer to grow backward.
options.feedback: The Add Buffer is always append-only.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Applying non-overlapping edits from highest offset to lowest keeps all preceding cursor offsets intact.

knowledgeChecks.question: A user opens a 10 MB minified JavaScript file consisting of a **single line**. How does the buffer avoid freezing the UI thread during scrolling?

options.text: It uses O(log P) offset slicing to fetch only the ~300 visible horizontal columns and disables regex tokenizers on lines >20K chars.
options.feedback: Correct! Horizontal viewport slicing + tokenizer line caps prevent O(N) string allocation and regex backtracking.

options.text: It inserts artificial newlines every 80 characters into the Original Buffer.
options.feedback: Mutating the user's file content silently would corrupt their source code.

options.text: It refuses to open any file smaller than 100 lines.
options.feedback: Minified files must still open and scroll smoothly.

options.text: It loads the file into a flat array instead of a Piece Tree.
options.feedback: A flat array still suffers O(N) shifts on edits.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: O(log P) horizontal column slicing and tokenizer length caps keep single-line 10 MB files at 60fps.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does background LSP/syntax indexing remain lock-free while the user types rapidly in the UI?

options.text: Immutable Original/Add buffers plus O(log P) path-copied tree roots give background workers a frozen snapshot with zero 100 MB copies.
options.feedback: Correct! Structural sharing lets workers read a consistent snapshot while UI edits advance a new root.

options.text: LSP workers read directly from the user's keyboard driver.
options.feedback: Workers read document text snapshots from the buffer.

options.text: The editor pauses all typing for 500 ms after every keystroke.
Undo stacks automatically broadcast diffs over WebSockets.
options.feedback: Local worker snapshots use in-memory tree structural sharing.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Structural sharing over immutable buffers provides O(log P) read snapshots without locking the UI thread.

beginner.summary: A fast code editor buffer keeps 100 MB files untouched in chunks, appends keystrokes to a scratchpad, and renders only the visible 60 lines.
beginner.keyTakeaway: Use a Piece Tree, apply multi-cursor edits bottom-up, and save via a temporary file so you never corrupt the open file.
beginner.byteSummary: To edit a 100 MB file at 60 frames per second, an editor never copies the whole file. It slices only the visible lines on screen, applies multi-cursor edits from bottom to top, and writes saves to a temporary file first.
